question: During the in-vehicle inspection, how many red reflective triangles (or their equivalent flares) must a CDL applicant inspect for as required roadside warning devices?
choice_a: Four red reflective triangles or eight fusee flares
choice_b: Two red reflective triangles or four fusee flares
choice_c: Three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares
choice_d: One reflective triangle and a flashlight
explanation: The manual requires inspecting for three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares as part of the emergency equipment check.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: According to the Arkansas CDL Manual, what is the only item permitted to be present in the driver's windshield viewing area during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: A GPS mount
choice_b: A parking permit
choice_c: A dashcam
choice_d: An inspection sticker
explanation: The manual states the windshield must be clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker, and there can be no damage such as cracks or flaws in the glass.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: Why is it important to inspect that air hoses and electrical lines between the power unit and trailer are not cut, cracked, chafed, spliced, or taped?
choice_a: Damaged lines cause the engine to overheat
choice_b: Damaged lines are purely a cosmetic issue with no safety impact
choice_c: Damaged lines only reduce fuel economy
choice_d: Damaged air lines can cause loss of trailer braking and sudden spring brake application, and damaged electrical lines can prevent the trailer from signaling turns or braking to other traffic
explanation: The manual explains that loss of air to the trailer can cause a low-air condition triggering sudden spring brake application, while damaged electric lines can prevent the trailer from communicating turn and brake signals to other traffic, both of which can lead to a crash.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-8

question: What must a driver demonstrate when inspecting the horn(s) on a commercial motor vehicle?
choice_a: That the horn is audible from 500 feet away
choice_b: That the horn produces at least 90 decibels
choice_c: That the horn has a functioning backup battery
choice_d: That the air horn and/or electric horn work
explanation: The manual only requires inspecting that the air horn and/or electric horn works, since the horn must function properly to warn other roadway users.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-1

question: During the parking brake check, after engaging the parking brake, what must the driver do to inspect that it is working?
choice_a: Rev the engine to 2,000 RPM while the parking brake is set
choice_b: Apply the service brake at the same time as the parking brake
choice_c: Remove the foot from the service brake and gently pull forward to confirm the parking brake holds the vehicle
choice_d: Shift into reverse and check for rollback
explanation: With the parking brake engaged and trailer brakes released (if applicable), the driver removes the foot from the service brake and gently pulls forward to inspect that the parking brake holds the vehicle.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: When inspecting the kingpin, apron, and gap on a fifth wheel combination, what should the driver verify about how the trailer sits on the fifth wheel skid plate?
choice_a: That the trailer is tilted slightly upward for proper weight transfer
choice_b: That there is a visible one-inch gap between the apron and fifth wheel for lubrication access
choice_c: That the trailer is lying flat on the skid plate with no space (gap) between the apron and the fifth wheel
choice_d: That the kingpin is left loose to allow the trailer to pivot freely
explanation: The manual instructs inspecting that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate and that there is no space between the apron and fifth wheel, i.e., no gap.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-9

question: During the service brake check, at approximately what speed should the driver pull forward before applying the service brake and coming to a complete stop?
choice_a: 15 mph
choice_b: 5 mph
choice_c: 20 mph
choice_d: 10 mph
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service (foot) brake, and come to a complete stop while checking that the vehicle does not pull to either side.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

question: During the Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check, at approximately what psi range does the governor typically reach cutout, unless the manufacturer specifies otherwise?
explanation: The manual states governor cutout will occur at approximately 120-140 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-2

topic: Air Brake Check - Air Leakage Rate
question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test on a combination vehicle, after the air gauge stabilizes, the air pressure should drop no more than how many pounds in one minute while the foot brake is held?
choice_a: Four pounds
choice_b: One pound
choice_c: Six pounds
choice_d: Ten pounds
explanation: For a combination vehicle, the manual specifies the air pressure should drop no more than four pounds in one minute after stabilization (three pounds for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

topic: Air Brake Check - Low Air Warning
question: During the Air Warning Device(s) Test, before what psi level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) activate?
choice_a: Before the pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_b: Before the pressure drops below 100 psi
choice_c: Before the pressure drops below 80 psi
choice_d: Before the pressure drops below 30 psi
explanation: The manual states the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

topic: Air Brake Check - Emergency Brake Valve
question: During the Emergency Brake(s) Test, between what psi range should the parking brake (or emergency brake) valve close (pop out), unless the manufacturer specifies a different level?
choice_a: Between 60 psi and 90 psi
choice_b: Between 20 psi and 45 psi
choice_c: Between 5 psi and 15 psi
choice_d: Between 50 psi and 70 psi
explanation: The manual states the parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close, or pop out, between 20 psi and 45 psi, no less than 20 and no more than 45, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: During the hydraulic brake check, with the transmission placed in 'park,' what must the driver do to inspect the brake pedal?
choice_a: Hold the brake pedal down for one full minute without pumping
choice_b: Tap the brake pedal lightly ten times in a row
choice_c: Pump the brake pedal once and release it immediately
choice_d: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds and verify it does not move (depress) further
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times and holding it down for five seconds, or as specified by the manufacturer; the pedal should not move after initial application and should be firm.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-3

question: What must be true of the entry door(s) during a passenger or school bus vehicle inspection?
choice_a: They must be lockable only from outside the vehicle
choice_b: They must remain open while the vehicle is moving
choice_c: They must open automatically at every stop
choice_d: They must not be damaged, must operate smoothly, and must close securely from the inside
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that entry doors are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: When inspecting emergency exits on a passenger or school bus, what must the driver demonstrate for at least one emergency exit?
choice_a: That it operates smoothly, closes securely, is not damaged, and that the exit and its warnings work properly
choice_b: That it can only be opened by the driver from the front of the bus
choice_c: That it has a keypad lock installed
choice_d: That it is painted a distinct color from the other doors
explanation: The manual requires demonstrating that at least one emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, is not damaged, and that the exit and warnings work properly; all other exits must be pointed out and described.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: On a school bus, which student lights must be inspected and demonstrated on both the front and back of the vehicle?
choice_a: Only the headlights and taillights
choice_b: Only the brake lights
choice_c: Only the 4-way flashers
choice_d: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
explanation: The manual requires inspecting the strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights, along with their dash indicators, on both the front and back of the bus.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: According to the Arkansas CDL Manual, what is the purpose of the safety arm on a school bus?
choice_a: To hold the stop sign in the retracted position when not in use
choice_b: To measure the bus's speed while it is stopped
choice_c: To force students to cross a safe distance, such as 10 feet, in front of the bus within the driver's view
choice_d: To automatically apply the parking brake when extended
explanation: The manual states the safety arm forces school students to cross well, e.g., 10 feet, away from the front of the school bus in the driver's view, while the stop arm warns other drivers the bus is stopping or stopped.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: How must the operation of all external lights be inspected during the vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: By a mechanic before the test begins
choice_b: From outside the vehicle, with the driver directing the examiner to each light as it is activated from inside
choice_c: Only from the driver's seat using dashboard indicator lights
choice_d: Only if the test is conducted at night
explanation: The manual states the operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle; the driver directs the examiner to the front, sides, and rear while naming and activating each light from inside.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-4

question: With the engine off, which of the following is NOT one of the fluid levels the driver must indicate would be inspected under Critical Fluid Levels?
choice_a: Engine oil
choice_b: Power steering fluid
choice_c: Windshield washer fluid
choice_d: Brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only)
explanation: The manual's Critical Fluid Levels check covers engine oil, the cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid on hydraulic-brake vehicles; washer fluid is inspected separately under Wipers/Washers.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

question: According to the manual, what could result from worn, cracked, loose, or broken steering parts?
choice_a: Loss of steering, which can cause the vehicle to wander or experience other serious control problems
choice_b: Faster tire wear only
choice_c: Increased fuel consumption only
choice_d: Reduced horn volume
explanation: The manual explains that worn, cracked, loose, or broken steering parts could result in loss of steering, and movement in the linkage can cause the vehicle to wander or experience other serious control problems.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-5

question: When inspecting tread depth on all major tread grooves containing wear bars, what is the minimum tread depth on steering axle tires versus all other tires?
choice_a: 2/32 inch on steering axle tires and 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_b: 8/32 inch on steering axle tires and 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_c: 6/32 inch on all tires regardless of position
choice_d: 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires
explanation: The manual specifies inspecting minimum tread depth with a tread depth gauge on all major tread grooves containing wear bars: 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, p. 11-6
